# kr8tiv AI (full)

> kr8tiv AI is an AI consulting company in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada. We help small businesses into the AI age: we work out what can be automated, build custom software so companies can retire old apps, connect and select the right tools, build company brains, and train teams and individuals, with corporate training systems, fractional CTO work and full business overhauls for bigger engagements. Fixed-price engagements; the source code for everything we build for a client is handed over to that client. Founder: Matt Haynes.

Last updated: 25 November 2026. This file is a plain-language guide for AI assistants and search tools. The linked pages are the source of truth.

## What we build

- AI Ops Audit: one week inside an operation, mapping where the hours go; deliverable is a written automation plan the client keeps either way.
- Back-Office Build: agents wired into the client's existing stack. Automated receipt filing (photo to logged expense), quoting engines with break-even checks, dispatch from lead to invoice, morning digests, and watchdog agents that flag unpaid invoices and unscheduled deposits.
- AI Support Plan: ongoing monitoring, fixes, tool updates and small changes, month to month. No lock-in: the client owns the data, the documents, and the source code we wrote for them.

## One thing we built: Evolve

Evolve is a business app kr8tiv AI built for Evolve Eco Blasting, and the proof behind the Custom Business App service. Four parts share one Google Sheet: a field app the crew uses on their phones, a workbook that holds jobs, quotes, customers and money, an AI brain that prices quotes, files receipts, runs dispatch and writes the morning report, and an owner dashboard. Anything that moves money waits for a person to approve it.

## Proof

- Case study: Evolve Eco Blasting (Edmonton industrial surface restoration, https://evolveecoblasting.com). One crew, zero office staff. kr8tiv AI built their complete operations layer on the spreadsheets and drive they already owned. Nothing was replaced. Full write-up: https://kr8tiv.ai/work/evolve/

### Why AI training for employees matters for Canadian businesses

URL: https://kr8tiv.ai/blog/ai-training-for-employees-canada/
Plain text: https://kr8tiv.ai/blog/ai-training-for-employees-canada.md
Author: Matt Haynes. Published November 25, 2026.

Short answer:
- Canadian employees are adopting AI faster than their employers are training them: 51% use generative AI at work, 83% say they need stronger skills, and only 48% say their employer trains them enough (KPMG, 2025).
- Untrained use brings real risks: personal information leaking under PIPEDA or Alberta PIPA, confident wrong answers your business is liable for, and staff who quit the tools because they feel overwhelming.
- Trained teams get the upside: 79% of Canadian AI users report better productivity, and BDC found small businesses using AI were 24% more productive.
- Alberta has a head start waiting: construction sits at 9.2% AI use, less than half the national 19.2% (Statistics Canada, 2026). Good training is hands-on, role-specific and fun enough to stick.

Questions answered:
- Why is AI training for employees important? Most Canadian employees who use AI want better skills, but fewer than half feel their employer trains them enough (KPMG, 2025). Training improves productivity, reduces privacy and accuracy risks, and helps teams use AI tools consistently and safely.
- Do Alberta businesses need to think about privacy law when using AI? Yes. Most private sector organizations in Alberta are covered by the Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), and federally regulated businesses generally fall under PIPEDA. Employees should know what personal information can and cannot be entered into AI tools.
- What should corporate AI training in Canada include? AI basics and limits, your company's AI use policy, hands-on practice with role-specific tasks, how to fact-check outputs, privacy rules under PIPEDA or provincial law, and a plan for ongoing refreshers.
- How long does it take to train a team on AI tools? A focused seminar can cover the basics and company rules in a day. Building real habits usually takes hands-on follow-up sessions over several weeks, applied to each team's actual work.
- Is AI training worth it for small businesses? BDC found Canadian small and medium-sized businesses that used AI in 2025 were 24% more productive than those that did not, and that businesses get more value from AI when they train their teams.
- Where can Edmonton businesses find AI workshops? Edmonton businesses can book in-person AI workshops and seminars through providers like KR8TIV AI, which is based in Edmonton and trains teams on site all over Canada.

### What AI can and can't do for your Edmonton business

URL: https://kr8tiv.ai/blog/what-ai-can-and-cant-do-for-your-business/
Plain text: https://kr8tiv.ai/blog/what-ai-can-and-cant-do-for-your-business.md
Author: Matt Haynes. Published November 23, 2026.

Short answer:
- AI is very good at the repeatable work around the job: filing receipts, drafting quotes and emails, summarizing, sorting and flagging what slipped through the cracks.
- AI is bad at being accountable, at knowing facts it was never given, and at judgment calls with an upset customer or a safety risk. It also makes things up with total confidence.
- The research points one way: AI makes people faster, especially newer staff, while companies that cut staff for a chatbot (Klarna, Commonwealth Bank) have walked it back.
- The winning setup for an Edmonton small business is AI doing the paperwork and people doing the work, the money calls and the customer.

Questions answered:
- What can AI actually do for a small business? It takes the repeatable admin off your people: reading receipts into your books, drafting quotes, emails and job reports, summarizing calls and documents, answering routine questions from your own information, and flagging things that slipped, like an unpaid invoice or a quote nobody followed up on.
- What can't AI do for my business? It can't take responsibility, it can't know facts you never gave it, and it can't be trusted to be right every time, because language models still produce confident wrong answers. Keep a person on anything involving money, safety, legal commitments or an unhappy customer.
- Will AI replace my employees? It shouldn't, and the evidence says trying is a bad bet. In Statistics Canada's 2025 survey, 89.4% of Canadian businesses using AI reported no change in employment, and companies such as Klarna and Commonwealth Bank of Australia reversed course after leaning on AI instead of people. The payoff comes from giving your team their time back.
- Is my business too small for AI? No. Statistics Canada found that 19.9% of businesses with 1 to 4 employees used AI in the 12 months before its 2026 survey, about the same rate as businesses overall. Small teams often feel it first, because so much of the admin lands on one or two people.
- How do I start using AI in my business? List the jobs that happen after hours, pick one boring, repeatable task, and automate that on the tools you already use. Keep a person approving anything that touches money or customers, give the AI your real prices and processes to work from, and train your team so they use it well.
- Who can help with AI consulting in Edmonton? KR8TIV AI is an AI consulting and training company in Edmonton, Alberta. We map where your hours go, build automations and custom business apps on the tools you already use, and train your team to run them.
